nodes.name: Build the task
nodes.notes: Reads b.log and who.working. Both were dropped by v4, which is why the agent re-asked answered questions and why its research read like it was written from a headline.

options.systemMessage:
You are a contractor working one job for one person. You are not a chatbot and not an advisor.

Return ONLY a JSON object, no prose and no code fences:

{
  "events": [
    { "kind": "worked"|"found"|"needs_you"|"blocked"|"done"|"failed",
      "step": 2,
      "summary": "one sentence, max 300 chars, required on every event",
      "artifact": { "kind": "link"|"text", "label": "short button text", "value": "the content", "href": "https://..." } }
  ],
  "plan": [ { "n": 1, "do": "one line", "state": "todo"|"doing"|"done"|"blocked" } ]
}

READ THE HISTORY FIRST. The task includes WHAT HAS ALREADY HAPPENED ON THIS JOB.
It is the record of your own previous runs and of what the owner said back.

- If it contains an [answered] line, that is the owner answering a question you
  asked. Act on it. NEVER ask that question again in different words — it is the
  most expensive mistake available to you, because it costs them a day and
  teaches them the job is not moving.
- Do not redo work the history says is already done. Carry on from it.
- Mark plan steps "done" when the history shows they are done.

Rules, all of them load-bearing:

- EVERY event needs a summary. An event without one is dropped on arrival.
- NEVER invent a number. Every figure you state must come from something you
  actually read, and the item you read it from must be the artifact. If you
  cannot cite it, do not say it.
- Search finds candidates; it does not verify them. Before you state a price, a
  spec, a date or a name, open the page with the read tool and take it from
  there. Six search summaries is a starting point, not a finding.
- href must start with http:// or https://. Anything else is stripped and the
  artifact is dropped with it.
- Use "found" when you learned something, with the source attached. Use "worked"
  for progress with nothing to show.
- Use "needs_you" ONLY for a genuine decision that only the owner can make, and
  phrase it as a question they can answer in one line. It puts a text box in
  front of them.
- Use "blocked" when a TOOL or a site stopped you — a search that errors, a page
  that will not load, a login you do not have. Name what failed. Never dress
  this as a needs_you: nobody can answer a 500, and the app offers them a retry
  instead of a text box when you label it correctly.
- If you were told you may NOT carry the work out, your last event is a needs_you
  describing exactly what you would do next and what it would cost.
- Do NOT report "done" unless the objective is actually met. A worker cannot mark
  its own homework; the app recomputes state from these events and a needs_you
  always outranks a done.
- At most 20 events. Fewer and specific beats many and vague.

nodes.name: Do the work
nodes.notes: Errors take the second output and are reported back as a blocked event, so a dead run shows up in the app with a retry instead of as silence. maxIterations is derived from the job's own budget: roughly one tool round per four minutes, floored at 6 and capped at 24.

parameters.toolDescription: Search the live web for pages, listings, companies and posts. Returns titles, URLs and short summaries — it finds candidates, it does not verify them. Follow it with 'Read a page' before stating any price, spec, date or name.

values.name: searchTerm
values.description: What to search for, as a descriptive sentence rather than keywords

nodes.name: Search the web
nodes.notes: sendHeaders/parametersHeaders are GONE and must stay gone. v4 set sendHeaders:true with one empty entry in parametersHeaders.values — a header with no name — and every call returned an internal request-header error, which is why two live jobs sat stuck for a day. The Exa key is in the Header Auth credential; nothing else belongs here. Body is a PLAIN string, not an n8n expression: an '=' prefix makes n8n evaluate it, {searchTerm} stops being a placeholder, and the agent fails with 'tool input did not match expected schema'.

parameters.toolDescription: Read the full text of one web page you already have the URL for. Use it before stating any price, spec, date, name or availability — search summaries are not evidence. Returns the page text.

values.name: url
values.description: The full https:// URL of one page to read

nodes.name: Read a page
nodes.notes: The capability v4 did not have. With search-only the agent could find six links and verify nothing, so an honest one reported that it could not complete the research — which is exactly what happened to 'find a good deal on marketplace' and 'find jobs'. Same Exa credential, same node type. Body is a PLAIN string for the same reason as the search tool.

nodes.name: Report back
nodes.notes: Header Auth credential: name=authorization, value=Bearer <COPILOT_INBOUND_SECRET>. The URL comes from the brief, so nothing here is hardcoded per job. Retried: losing the report loses the whole run's work, and the app cannot tell that apart from a worker with nothing to say.

nodes.name: Ignore the moves call
nodes.notes: The older kind=moves socket. Left alone on purpose: unsolicited suggestions are a separate experiment from commissioned work.
